study_identification_part.si_4_title: Revealing Individual Neuroanatomical Heterogeneity in Alzheimer Disease Using Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: A hierarchical Bayesian regression model was trained on multisite data to generate normative models per region. The model adaptively pools parameter estimates across sites via a shared prior over regression parameters. PCNtoolkit (version 0.20) was used for all modeling steps.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: A hierarchical Bayesian regression model was trained on multisite data to generate normative models per region using the covariates age and sex. This was based on the population variation in the reference data set (training data), which adaptively pools parameter estimates across sites via a shared prior over regression parameters across sites.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness measurements across 148 brain regions were obtained from T1-weighted MRI scans. Cortical thickness values were generated using FreeSurfer's recon-all cross-sectional approach based on the Destrieux atlas (148 regions plus mean cortical thickness).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cortical thickness measurements across 148 brain regions were obtained from T1-weighted MRI scans from 62 sites of the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative... Cortical thickness values were generated using the recon-all cross-sectional approach. This cortical thickness algorithm calculates the mean distance between vertices of a corrected, triangulated estimated gray/white matter surface and gray matter/CSF (pial) surface, which generated the cortical thickness of each region of the Destrieux atlas regions.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Verdi2023.pdf.md: Abstract; Methods / Estimation of Cortical Thickness

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as primary covariates in the normative model. Site variation was handled through hierarchical Bayesian framework with shared priors across sites.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: A hierarchical Bayesian regression model was trained on multisite data to generate normative models per region using the covariates age and sex... which adaptively pools parameter estimates across sites via a shared prior over regression parameters across sites. This simultaneously accounts for intersite variation and allows sites to borrow strength from one another in a fully Bayesian framework.
